To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the direct activation of actomyosin- ATP-ase and oxidative phosporylation is the main mechanism which causes an increase in ATP production and a decrease in ATP/ADp ratio in response to the increased energy demand during muscle contractions.
the direct activation of actomyosin- ATP-ase and of oxidative phosphorylation is the main mechanism of fitting of ATP production rate to ATP consumption rate during muscle contraction.

the rate of oxidative phosphorylation during muscle contraction should be regulated by a direct activation of most steps, not by a negative feedback, and that the activator should stimulate the actinomyosine-ATPase, oxidative phosphorylation, and possibly also other processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how the rate and efficiency of ATP production by the respiratory chain are controlled in order to fit them to the energy demand during contraction.
the question of how ATP production by oxidative phosporylation is regulated to meet the increased energy demand during muscle contractions.
a theoretical study of the regulation of the rate of ATP supply during maximal work.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rate of ATP supply during the muscle contraction is regulated by a complex regulatory mechanism which includes the direct activation of most of the oxidative-phosphorylation steps by an external factor, and a negative feedback via the ADP concentration.
the parallel stimulation of actinomy-osin-ATPase and oxidative phosphorylating enzymes is the main mechanism for regulation of ATP supply during maximal muscle work.
the rate of ATP supply during the muscle contraction is regulated by the direct activation of the oxidative phosphorylating system by an external efflector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of oxidative phosphorylation is a complex process involving a large number of enzymes and processes, and that the regulation of the respiration rate is not a simple process.
the regulation of ATP supply during the muscle contraction can be described in the following way.

a great increase in the rate of ATP supply during the onset of maximal muscular work is achieved by a parallel direct activation of different enzymes/process steps by a single external activator, which is not a product or a metabolite of the metabolic pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of ATP supply during contraction is not a simple process.
the direct activation of different enzymes/process is a more efficient way of regulation of ATP supply than the indirect activation via changes in ADP and ATP/ADPs ratios.
the regulation of oxidative phosphorylation is much more complex than it was thought previously.
